result:
Fix complete, minimal one-line diff plus the new regression test.

**What was wrong:** `POST /process/{session_id}` (routes.py:333) called `explainer.explain(doc, classification, lang)` with 3 args, but `ExplainerAgent.explain()` only accepts `(text, language)` — a prior refactor tightened the signature and this call site wasn't updated, causing every `/process` request to raise a `TypeError` (caught by `_endpoint_guard` and surfaced as a 500). I checked `risk_scanner.scan()` in the same `asyncio.gather` block and confirmed its signature is still `(document, classification, lang)`, matching its call site exactly — no fix needed there. I also found `wills_trusts.py`'s `_explainer.explain(...)` call, but that uses an unrelated `WillsTrustsExplainer` class, out of scope for this defect.

**What changed:** `explainer.explain(doc, classification, lang)` → `explainer.explain(document_text, lang)`, using the raw document text already in hand as `doc_record["document_text"]`. Added `backend/tests/test_process_endpoint.py`, which mocks `db`, `classifier`, `explainer`, `risk_scanner`, and `escalation_router` to call `process_document` directly and assert `explain` is awaited with `(document_text, "en")` — it failed against the old code (`TypeError`-triggering wrong-arity call captured via mock) and passes now. Full CI-scope suite: 197 passed, 1 skipped.

**What could regress:** none expected — the fix only narrows the arguments passed to an existing, unmodified method, and no other caller relies on the old call site's classification context being passed to `explain`.
